path_name: next/link no longer requires nested <a> tag in Next.js 13+
description: Starting in Next.js 13, the Link component automatically renders an <a> tag and no longer requires (or allows) a manually nested <a> child element. Applications with nested <a> tags inside Link components may experience rendering issues or hydration errors. The legacyBehavior prop can be used for backward compatibility, or a codemod can automatically update the code.

conditions.statement: Target Next.js version is 13.x or higher

evidence.quote_or_summary: In Next.js 13, `<Link>` always renders an `<a>` and allows you to forward props to the underlying tag.
evidence.relevance: Documents the Link behavior change in Next.js 13

evidence.quote_or_summary: The `next/link` child can no longer be `<a>`. Add the `legacyBehavior` prop to use the legacy behavior or remove the `<a>` to upgrade. A codemod is available to automatically upgrade your code.
evidence.relevance: Confirms this is a breaking change affecting Next.js 13+

conditions.statement: Application has Link components with nested <a> tags

evidence.quote_or_summary: Next.js 12: `<a>` has to be nested otherwise it's excluded. Next.js 13: `<Link>` always renders `<a>`
evidence.relevance: Shows the pattern that needs to be changed

suggested_actions: Search codebase for Link components with nested anchor tags: grep -r "<Link" --include="*.jsx" --include="*.tsx" | grep "<a"
Run the automated codemod: npx @next/codemod new-link ./
Manually review Link components to ensure <a> tags are removed and props are moved to Link
Alternatively, add legacyBehavior prop to preserve old behavior temporarily: <Link legacyBehavior>
Test all navigation links after migration to ensure proper routing and styling
